counterfactual_missing_items: No evidence of alternative spinal pathology such as malignancy or fracture
No mention of neurological deficit pattern inconsistent with discitis
No negative imaging or culture results to refute infection
decisive_items: MRI of the lumbar spine demonstrated decreased T1 signal and increased T2 and STIR signal at L4–L5
lumbar spinal tenderness and bilateral leg weakness without sensory loss
response.rationale: R5 integrates the acute presentation (back pain, fever, leg weakness), laboratory inflammation, positive blood cultures, and characteristic MRI findings into a cohesive diagnosis of spondylodiscitis. R1 identifies the pathogen but lacks the anatomical and imaging specificity. R7 and R2 refer to prior conditions not explaining the current acute spinal syndrome.

rejected.why: Esophageal cancer is the underlying history but does not explain the acute lumbar symptoms and MRI changes.
Anastomotic fistula was a prior complication, not the current presentation of back pain and spinal imaging findings.
